thread:
anya: Kicking off onboarding for the new atlas-13b run — need to pick a quantization path and calibration plan. Main constraints: keep end-user quality drop <~1% on our long-form benchmark, but target >=30% token-cost reduction. Thoughts?
vikram: Quick summary: int8 (per-channel) = safest, good latency wins; fp8 = promising for latency + quality but harder to standardize; gguf + dynamic matmul kernels gives best size reduction for hosted cache, but calibration/format tooling still evolving.
maggie: Can we define a short acceptance checklist for the bring-up? e.g., top-1/ROUGE drop thresholds, instruction-following sanity checks, and hallucination regression quick scan.
anya: Yup — initial checklist I propose: 1) generation-level pass on our full eval set (1000 prompts) compare ROUGE/ExactMatch; 2) 5-shot instruction probe for safety regressions; 3) latency p50/p95 on dedicated 1xA10; 4) cost simulation using our billing model. If any model misses quality thresholds, reject.
vikram: For calibration runs, I recommend two phased sweeps: calibration-only (small shards, 8 seeds) to find stable scales, then a sensitivity sweep (vary clip/percentile, per-channel vs per-tensor) with representative prompts. We should capture: token-level cross-entropy delta, SAMPLING BLEU/ROUGE, and a few deterministic evals (exact match).
anya: I'll attach the quick calib command I'm going to use — feel free to copy/run: 
```bash
# sample calibration run
python infra/calibrate.py \
  --model atlas-13b \
  --format gguf \
  --scheme awq_perchannel \
  --calib-path s3://redwood-eval/atlas/calib/seed-42.jsonl \
  --batch-size 64 \
  --quant-bits 8 \
  --out out/atlas_gguf_awq.pth
```
vikram: Add `--collect-kv-stats` for the first pass so we can inspect activation distributions. Also set `--fake-quant` to validate without writing artifacts.
maggie: For acceptance thresholds: allow up to 1% absolute ROUGE-L drop OR <=2% relative cross-entropy increase; anything beyond needs an A/B with canary traffic. Also add a manual check for safety prompt set (we have a 200-prompt safety suite).
quant-bot: calib-run finished: format=gguf bits=8 scheme=awq_perchannel seed=42 samples=1024 -> avg_xent_delta=0.018 (1.8%) ; rougeL_drop=0.9% ; p95_latency_delta=-12% ; size_reduction=3.8x. Artifacts: s3://redwood-eval/atlas/out/atlas_gguf_awq_seed42/
olivia: Nice. For Dedicated capacity: I can reserve 2xA10 for overnight runs (11pm-7am UTC) and a small canary slot at 2pm. Cost estimate for full sweep (calib+sensitivity) ~ $420/day on Dedicated, hosted sim ~ $780/day.
sam: For canary rollout: stage -> 1% traffic for 6h -> health check on loss/regressions -> 5% for 12h -> failover to baseline if cross-entropy jumps >1.5% or safety hits >0.5% regressions. Instrument alerts: per-route perf, hallucination signals, error-rate.
vikram: We should also try an fp8 pilot on a single shard: fp8-e4m3 with per-channel scaling gave good results on similar 13B in our past tests. It’s trickier to support across runtimes, but worth exploring for 2-3% extra cost savings.
maggie: Agree. Proposed plan: 1) Run gguf-awq int8 baseline (full sweep). 2) If baseline meets thresholds, run fp8 pilot on a subset of prompts and compare. 3) If fp8 improves cost w/o quality regression, escalate to canary.
anya: I'll kick off the gguf baseline sweep tonight with seeds [42,101,202] and shared calib shards. Vikram — can you add `--kv-cache-test` to the sensitivity sweep? We want to ensure online decoding latencies behave.
vikram: Yup. Also logging: add `--trace-token` for a few flame-sampled requests so we can inspect kernel-level hotspots.
quant-bot: sensitivity-sweep queued with params: seeds=[42,101,202], clip_pct=[99.9,99.5,99.0], perchannel=[true,false], collect_kv=true. Expected finish: ~7h.
maggie: Add a small human-review step after initial sweep: pick 20 random prompts from each quartile and have an evaluator thumbs-up/bad output tagging — will help detect subtle instruction drift.
olivia: One more: if we take the gguf path, ensure our importer script updates model catalog with `quant_profile` metadata so Optimize recommendations consider it. I can PR a small schema change.
anya: Action items: 1) anya to run gguf baseline sweep tonight (seeds posted). 2) vikram to enable kv-traces and collect_kv. 3) maggie to prepare human-review set & scoring sheet. 4) olivia to reserve Dedicated capacity and PR catalog change. 5) sam to wire canary alerts.
anya: Thanks all — will post results in this thread (and link to s3 artifacts). :rocket:
